summary: Most probable root cause: a synchronized TTL-expiry burst in redis-cache. About 8000 hot keys expired within one second, repeatedly, from 15:10:14 until 15:44:54. This was not memory-pressure eviction. The hit ratio fell to 0.35, portfolio-svc reads fell through to postgres, the postgres pool backed up (pool_waiting up to 35), and portfolio-svc latency (and the web-app latency above it) rose from 15:11. Recovery at 15:45 coincides with the bursts stopping. Balance answers depend on portfolio-svc and share this path, but orchestrator and llm-gateway latency showed no step, so llm-gateway is not supported as a cause. The reason the hot keys expire together (shared TTLs, a re-warm at one time) is not established, and the postgres-first alternative (H2) is not fully excluded, because the first postgres slow-query WARN (15:10:02) precedes the first redis burst log (15:10:14).

hypotheses.statement: redis-cache lost about 8000 hot keys in synchronized TTL-expiry bursts from 15:10:14, which is not memory-pressure eviction; the hit ratio fell to 0.35, portfolio-svc reads fell through to postgres, the pool backed up and portfolio-svc latency rose from 15:11 until the bursts stopped at 15:45.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: redis-cache logged 8000 hot keys expiring by TTL within one second at 15:10:14, matching the evicted_keys jump from 0 to 8000 and the hit_ratio drop at 15:10. Memory stayed at 55-60%, so this was not memory-pressure eviction.

About 20 further 8000-key bursts followed through 15:19, and the pattern continued until 15:44:54. Hit ratio sat at its 0.35 floor from 15:12 to 15:44 and evicted_keys and hit_ratio both returned to normal at 15:45, tracking the incident window.

Postgres pool_waiting rose from 0 at 15:10 to 35 by 15:13, and portfolio-svc latency first clearly departed from its band at 15:11, a minute after the cache and pool onset. Portfolio-svc latency returned to baseline at 15:45, consistent with a cache-driven cause. Redis request rate was flat, so the bursts were not driven by a traffic surge.

It is likely that the cache misses pushed holdings reads from portfolio-svc onto postgres. This fits with flat request volume and postgres rps, which points to added per-query cost rather than extra load. This is an assumption, as the sequence within the 15:10 minute is unresolved.
A past incident (INC-0412) had a similar mechanism (cache stampede on portfolio-svc, with late balance notifications), though it was caused by a Redis restart and is only a historical hint.

contradicting.text: The maxmemory policy and whether evicted_keys counts these TTL expiries are unverified, and the metric meaning is unclear. The flat plateaus (hit_ratio exactly 0.35, evicted_keys exactly 8000) could be exporter artifacts, and hit_ratio values above 1.0 show a data-quality problem.

The cause of the synchronized expiry is unknown. No config or deploy change was found for redis-cache or portfolio-svc, and INC-0412 involved a restart, which was not found. Redis slowlog warnings were already present before onset (from 14:37 and 14:59), and it is unclear whether they are cause or effect.
The first postgres slow-query WARN (15:10:02) precedes the first redis burst log (15:10:14), so the order is not proven. Clock skew is not excluded.

hypotheses.statement: postgres connection-pool contention or slow queries began independently at 15:10 (the first slow-query WARN is at 15:10:02), slowing portfolio-svc, its heaviest callee at 0.8; the cache dip would then be a secondary effect.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: Postgres logged its first slow-query WARN at 15:10:02 and the first pool-wait line at 15:10:04, ahead of the first redis burst log at 15:10:14. Postgres latency stepped up at 15:10 and ramped to 51 ms by 15:15.

contradicting.text: There is no independent postgres trigger. Postgres request rate was flat, logs before 15:10 show only routine checkpoints, and aa-sync looked routine. The only postgres-related deploy was a metrics label rename (likely observability-only, though its diff was not retrievable). The sub-minute ordering is within the noise of the redis onset, so a secondary effect of the cache misses is more likely.

hypotheses.statement: llm-gateway, or the upstream LLM provider, is slow independently of the portfolio problem, which would explain slow balance answers on the orchestrator to llm-gateway path while portfolio pages are slowed separately.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: llm-gateway latency and error rate showed no step at 15:10 and stayed in the same band. Orchestrator latency also did not move, so these hops do not explain the slowdown on the mean-level series.
Only mean-level series were available, so a tail (p95/p99) effect or provider-side issue is not ruled out. This is an assumption, not an established finding.

assumptions.text: Redis and postgres both move at the 15:10 minute, so their order within that minute is unresolved. The postgres pool-wait ramp (15:10–15:13) and the portfolio-svc rise at 15:11 are consistent with cache misses pushing reads onto postgres, but this is not proven.

The redis log says 'ttl expiry' and the metric says 'evicted_keys'. Both may describe the same 8000-key event, or they may be different mechanisms. The maxmemory policy and whether these are true evictions is unverified; memory_pct max 59.907 argues against memory-pressure eviction.
Balance-answer slowness is not visible in orchestrator or llm-gateway latency, so the llm-gateway and orchestrator hops are unlikely to explain it on the basis of these series alone.
The postgres-00591 label rename is probably observability-only, but the diff was not retrievable with my tools, so this is unverified. The tool only returned the note text.

The flat plateaus (hit_ratio exactly 0.35 for 33 minutes, evicted_keys exactly 8000.0 for 35 minutes) and the abrupt step back at 15:45 could come from exporter or stale-value behaviour rather than real cache state. This is unverified.

The synchronised expiry of about 8000 hot keys from 15:10 onward likely caused cache misses that pushed reads onto postgres and portfolio-svc. This would be a stampede of the INC-0412 type, but it is not yet confirmed.

The orchestrator and llm-gateway hops, measured by mean latency, do not explain the balance-answer slowdown by themselves. The balance symptom may come from a tail (p95/p99) or from a hop not measured here, but this is inferred from mean-level series only.

The 15:10 postgres contention most likely comes from cache misses (redis hit_ratio drop at 15:10 and floor at 15:12, per E-067/E-068) sending holdings lookups to postgres. The hit_ratio series was not pulled in this task, so the timing correlation with the pool ramp is unverified.
aa-sync is unlikely to be the postgres trigger (weakens E-065): its fetch/publish cadence looks routine in 15:00-15:14. There is no pre-15:00 baseline, so this is only a weak signal.

Latency rose with flat request volume, which fits added per-query cost (for example cache misses sending reads to postgres) more than extra read load. Unverified, since per-query cost is not measured here.

actions.text: Confirm the cache is currently healthy (hit_ratio, evicted_keys, pool_waiting) and check whether the TTL-expiry bursts could return. If they recur, pre-warm the hot keys as was done for INC-0412.
actions.rationale: Metrics show recovery at 15:45, but the cause of the bursts is unresolved, so a recurrence is possible. Pre-warming was the fix for the similar INC-0412.

actions.text: Find out why about 8000 hot keys expire at once. Check the TTLs set by portfolio-svc, whether the keys were written or re-warmed together (around 14:25-14:35), and the maxmemory policy. Add TTL jitter (randomized expiry) to hot keys.
actions.rationale: Synchronized TTL expiry is the proposed mechanism, but no tool exposed TTL values or writers, so it is not yet proven. Jitter prevents simultaneous expiry.

actions.text: Add stampede protection on portfolio-svc cache reads (request coalescing or a lock on miss, plus stale-while-revalidate), and consider a postgres pool-wait alert.
actions.rationale: Cache misses fell through to postgres, pool_waiting reached 35, and portfolio-svc is the shared path for both symptoms.

actions.text: Resolve the ordering and verify the mechanism: pull per-minute and sub-minute redis and postgres series, check redis INFO-level logs and uptime for a restart, and check whether evicted_keys counts TTL expiries. Check the 15:15-16:00 change window for redis-cache.
actions.rationale: The ordering between postgres and redis within the 15:10 minute is unresolved, and the config check for redis-cache stops at 15:15.
